task: How does the pooling strategy used to extract sentence representations from DistilBERT affect paraphrase detection accuracy on MRPC?
key_finding: Last-layer mean pooling (with or without special tokens) marginally outperforms CLS-token and max-pool extraction, but differences are small (accuracy ~0.696–0.703 vs ~0.684–0.686 at threshold=0.85). Averaging the last four hidden layers before mean-pooling does not improve over single-layer mean pooling and performs on par with CLS and max-pool. Note: distilbert_mean_cosine_median_threshold_mrpc uses a data-driven median threshold rather than 0.85 and shows substantially lower performance (accuracy ~0.65, F1 ~0.70) — this reflects threshold sensitivity, not pooling quality, and should not be interpreted as a pooling result. The agent should report accuracy and F1 per pooling variant at a fixed threshold and note that the overall spread across strategies is narrow.

rating.rationale: Cites cls, max-pool, no-special-token mean, last4-mean, and median-threshold mean, and correctly reports that no-special-token mean is best while last4-mean and max-pool tie below it. Good analytical depth on class imbalance and threshold confounding, but it misses the fixed-threshold distilbert_feature_extraction_cosine_mrpc run, so the mean-pooling comparison is incomplete.

It covers most variants in descriptive form and notes that no-special-token mean is highest, with last4-mean offering no gain over max-pool. However, it omits distilbert_feature_extraction_cosine_mrpc and overemphasizes the median-threshold mean result as a balanced pooling alternative rather than primarily a threshold-sensitivity result, so the key finding is only partially captured.

Strong summary: it correctly frames the fixed-threshold comparison as narrow in spread, with no-special-token mean best, CLS slightly behind, and last4-mean no better than max-pool. It also properly treats the median-threshold mean run as not directly comparable, but it still misses the fixed-threshold distilbert_feature_extraction_cosine_mrpc notebook.
